### Airhead Composting Toilet

> So, the solids tank can take, on average 80 uses. So, if 2 people use the toilet every day, it will last 1 month. But if 2 people are only using it at weekends, it can easily last a full season. Of course it can be emptied more frequently if you are happy to do so.
> 
> For liquids it will also depend on usage. But, for 2 people, the small tank will need to be emptied every 1-2 days, and the large tank will last 2-4 days.

> Carry these three (the road-trip essentials):
DEF / AdBlue — the most important one. This diesel uses a DEF system, and if it runs dry you get escalating warnings and eventually the van won't restart. Carry a 2.5-gallon jug and top off when the dash prompts you. Good news: DEF is fully standardized (ISO 22241), so any brand — BlueDEF, Peak, store brand — is identical. This is the one fluid where brand genuinely doesn't matter.
> Engine oil — 1–2 quarts, but the right spec. It needs full-synthetic low-SAPS oil meeting Mercedes MB 229.52 (or at minimum 229.51), 5W-30, because the low-ash formulation protects the diesel particulate filter. The catch that makes carrying it essential: 229.52 is notoriously hard to find off the shelf — "like hens' teeth," realistically not stocked at most gas stations or truck stops, and common diesel oils like Rotella don't carry the rating. So buy a couple quarts of Mobil 1 ESP, Liqui Moly Top Tec 4600, or similar before you go — for topping off only. Don't grab generic diesel oil at a truck stop in a pinch; it can harm the DPF. 
> Coolant — match the color in the reservoir. A 2018 Sprinter uses the MB 325.6 / G40 pink coolant (the spec for all 2014-and-later Sprinters), not the older blue. Carry a jug (premixed 50/50, or concentrate cut with distilled water) of the matching pink spec — Genuine MB or Zerex G40 — and never mix pink and blue or top with random green stuff. For a hot-desert-plus-mountain-pass trip, having coolant on hand is genuinely worth it.
> Nice to carry, low priority:
> Washer fluid (cheap, and you'll go through it on bug-and-dust-covered windshields — buy anywhere). And a small bottle of DOT 4 brake fluid (ATE Type 200 exceeds DOT 4) for the mountain descents — though if you actually need to add brake fluid, that signals pad wear or a leak, so it's emergency-only, not routine.

# RV Guide (from the owner)

## Arriving

Van parking: Location 📍

The key is in the magnetic keybox under the van (details later).

- **Fuel: ONLY DIESEL N2, no bio diesel.**
- Fill the water: Location 📍. Open back doors, find a hose in the water tank box, screw on the hose and fill the tank. (There is a water indicator inside the van so you can see how much water you have.)
- Turn on the water pump after filling the fresh water — you'll hear it start working. Above the back bench seats. **It should be on all the time you live in the van.**

> [Image missing: IMG_2710.jpeg]

- 1 — water heater
- 2 — water pump (always on)
- 3 — W — grey water tank dump

**Indicators:**

- Left — fresh water meter
- Right — battery charge

## Toilet — Air Head Classic

> [Image missing: IMG_2610.jpeg]

### Number 1: urine container

> [Image missing: IMG_2609.jpeg]

You just pour a bit of enzyme into the empty container and empty it daily into any public toilet. Buy a special bag that you can carry it in 😂

### Number 2

Wear rubber gloves we have in drawer 2.

**Composting part.** Detach the grey hose (red arrow points where) on the side and take the whole toilet outside.

Unscrew and twist the top part to remove it.

> [Image missing: IMG_2611.jpeg]

Take a trash bag, put one block of coco coir in, and add water until it turns into a soil. It should be not too wet and not too dry, just a bit moist. When there are no lumps and the coir is consistent in texture, fill the composting toilet half way, so when you use a pedal to mix it moves with ease.

Close the lid, screw everything back, put the toilet back, and attach the grey hose.

All done!

## Dumping grey water

As you see you've used around half of your water, it's time to dump the grey water (the grey water tank is smaller than the fresh water tank).

Find a dumping station in the **iOverlander** app or at campgrounds.

The tank is on the driver's side, so drive close to the dumping hole and when ready to dump turn the black switch with **W** on it (above the back bench seats).

Wait until the water stops running. Turn off the switch.

## Electricity

**No inverter (always works):**

- Puck lights
- USB outlets

**Inverter:**

- Regular outlets
- Water heater
- Induction stove

### Inverter app: VictronConnect

- Load the app.
- The connection is bluetooth.
- It will ask for a PIN code.
- **PIN: 474747**
- Now you should be connected.
- To turn on and off: text us to find out what is what 🫠

### Induction stove

1. Turn on the inverter.
2. There is a white switch on the side of the counter, left of the stove — turn it on.
3. Hear a beep.
4. Turn on.
5. Choose the burner.
6. Choose the heat level.
7. When not in use, turn off the inverter.

### Heating water

1. Turn on the inverter.
2. Turn on the white switch above the seats.
3. Wait around 10 minutes.
4. Hot water can take some time to move through the pipes — don't be discouraged.

## Useful

In San Diego: park anywhere in the Pacific Beach residential area.

### Apps

- **iOverlander** — places to stop for the night, water, camping, dumping stations. Use filters to choose what you need.
- **Park4night** — parking for the night.

### Tips

- Before driving, make sure drawers are closed — they're quite noisy if left open.
- If you park uphill, sleep with your heads toward the front of the van, and vice versa. **Really matters.**
- When it gets dark and there's light in the van, it's time to put the reflectix on the windows so nobody sees you. We have one for a big window and two for the small ones in the sleeping area.
- There's supposed to be a table between the two bench seats, but it's not installed. Call Nick and he will explain how to do it — it's very easy, so you can have meals conveniently in the van. We removed it because of Lola.

### Wash tubs

There are two foldable wash tubs behind the driver's seat on the floor:

> [Image missing: IMG_2718.jpeg]

- **Black/grey** — for dishes. If you have to drive and have no time to wash the dishes, just fully unfold the tub, put the dishes in, and put the tub in the sink — it fits very well so dishes won't fly around and make noise in the metal sink. Also can soak dishes in there.
- **White/grey** — if you want to hand-wash laundry, do it in this tub.

### Detachable lights

We have a few lights that are detachable and can be placed in different areas of the van.
